\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پیٹنا} (pīṭnā)}{پیٹنا (pīṭnā)}]{\ur{پیٹنا} (pīṭnā) — to beat}

\label{lesson:UR-C307-pitna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to shudder, then the Urdu for a shock.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پیٹنا}}
\textbf{\ur{پیٹنا}} — \emph{pīṭnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to beat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{لوگوں} \ur{نے} \ur{چور} \ur{کو} \ur{پیٹا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{logoṅ ne chor ko pīṭā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People beat the thief.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{دروازہ} \ur{پیٹا}, \emph{us ne darvāzā pīṭā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{pīṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to beat\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{piṭṭayati}, \textquotedblleft{}pounds\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8165). You can \textbf{\ur{پیٹنا}} a person, a drum or a door.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pīṭnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pīṭnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{logoṅ ne chor ko pīṭā.} — People beat the thief.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to shudder, then the Urdu for a shock, then say \emph{pīṭnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{پیٹنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To beat\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اینٹھنا} (ainṭhnā)}{اینٹھنا (ainṭhnā)}]{\ur{اینٹھنا} (ainṭhnā) — to twist; to wring}

\label{lesson:UR-C307-ainthna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a punch, then the Urdu for a slap.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اینٹھنا}}
\textbf{\ur{اینٹھنا}} — \emph{ainṭhnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to twist; to wring\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{رسی} \ur{اینٹھی}, \emph{us ne rassī ainṭhī}.

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from The Morning News to A Fight in the Market}

\label{lesson:UR-R307-review-300-307}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for a radio and to broadcast.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a radio, to broadcast, a headline, an official notice, a sensation
  \item a journalist, the scene of an event, an editor, a detail, to have written down
  \item a rumour, talk of the town, terror, to stir up, the public
  \item to deny, an admission, to put off, information, the reality
  \item a riot, an uproar, to break out, a police baton, a curfew
  \item a mystery, an informer, a guess, to be startled, a revelation
  \item a blast, a bomb, to echo, to shudder, a shock
  \item to beat, a scuffle, a punch, a slap, to twist
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A radio? (\textbf{\ur{ریڈیو}}, \emph{reḍiyo}.) To broadcast? (\textbf{\ur{نشر} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{nashr karnā}.) A headline? (\textbf{\ur{سرخی}}, \emph{surkhī}.) An official notice? (\textbf{\ur{اطلاع}}, \emph{ittilā}.) A sensation? (\textbf{\ur{سنسنی}}, \emph{sansanī}.) A journalist? (\textbf{\ur{صحافی}}, \emph{sahāfī}.) The scene of an event? (\textbf{\ur{موقع}}, \emph{mauqa}.) An editor? (\textbf{\ur{ایڈیٹر}}, \emph{eḍīṭar}.) A detail? (\textbf{\ur{تفصیل}}, \emph{tafsīl}.) To have written down? (\textbf{\ur{لکھوانا}}, \emph{likhvānā}.) A rumour? (\textbf{\ur{افواہ}}, \emph{afvāh}.) Talk of the town? (\textbf{\ur{چرچا}}, \emph{charchā}.) Terror? (\textbf{\ur{دہشت}}, \emph{dahshat}.) To stir up? (\textbf{\ur{بھڑکانا}}, \emph{bhaṛkānā}.) The public? (\textbf{\ur{عوام}}, \emph{avām}.) To deny? (\textbf{\ur{انکار} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{inkār karnā}.) An admission? (\textbf{\ur{اقرار}}, \emph{iqrār}.) To put off? (\textbf{\ur{ٹالنا}}, \emph{ṭālnā}.) Information? (\textbf{\ur{معلومات}}, \emph{mālūmāt}.) The reality? (\textbf{\ur{حقیقت}}, \emph{haqīqat}.) A riot? (\textbf{\ur{فساد}}, \emph{fasād}.) An uproar? (\textbf{\ur{ہنگامہ}}, \emph{hangāmā}.) To break out? (\textbf{\ur{پھوٹنا}}, \emph{phūṭnā}.) A police baton? (\textbf{\ur{لاٹھی}}, \emph{lāṭhī}.) A curfew? (\textbf{\ur{کرفیو}}, \emph{karfyū}.) A mystery? (\textbf{\ur{معمہ}}, \emph{muammā}.) An informer? (\textbf{\ur{مخبر}}, \emph{mukhbir}.) A guess? (\textbf{\ur{اندازہ}}, \emph{andāzā}.) To be startled? (\textbf{\ur{چونکنا}}, \emph{chaunknā}.) A revelation? (\textbf{\ur{انکشاف}}, \emph{inkishāf}.) A blast? (\textbf{\ur{دھماکا}}, \emph{dhamākā}.) A bomb? (\textbf{\ur{بم}}, \emph{bam}.) To echo? (\textbf{\ur{گونجنا}}, \emph{gūnjnā}.) To shudder? (\textbf{\ur{تھرانا}}, \emph{tharrānā}.) A shock? (\textbf{\ur{صدمہ}}, \emph{sadmā}.) To beat? (\textbf{\ur{پیٹنا}}, \emph{pīṭnā}.) A scuffle? (\textbf{\ur{جھڑپ}}, \emph{jhaṛap}.) A punch? (\textbf{\ur{گھونسا}}, \emph{ghūnsā}.) A slap? (\textbf{\ur{تھپڑ}}, \emph{thappaṛ}.) To twist? (\textbf{\ur{اینٹھنا}}, \emph{ainṭhnā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
